a201.text: Last time, we sorted living things into four groups. Today, we zoom in on one group. Animals!

a203.text: A frog, a bird and a fish. All at one pond! Are they one group?

a204.text: Did you lock in your answer? One group, or three? Hold on to it.

a302.text: It's You against the Buddies. You lock in first. One finger for every point. A little duck is hiding in this video. Can you spot it?

a401.text: Round Zero. A warm-up! A plant makes its own food. Can an animal? One, yes. Two, no. Show me with your fingers.

a404.text: Animals are unable to make their own food. They depend on other living things for food.

g103.text: What makes a frog an amphibian.

h501.text: Are you ready? Three! Two! One! Go!

a501.text: So, what is an animal? Look at the frog. A head. A body. And limbs. Its legs are its limbs.

a503.text: Animals are living things that usually have parts such as a head, a body and limbs.

a601.text: Some animals live only on land, while some live only in water. There are also some animals that can live both on land and in water.

a602.text: Animals have different outer coverings as they live in different places.

a701.text: Scientists have grouped the diversity of animals around us according to their similarities and differences.

a702.text: They use things we can see or measure. These are called observable characteristics.

a801.text: Round one. This frog sits on a leaf. Then, splash! It swims. Where can a frog live? One, only on land. Two, only in water. Three, both. Show me with your fingers.

a803.text: Two! It swims so well. It must live in water.

a804.text: Three. I saw it on a leaf, and in the pond.

a805.text: Three! It hops, and it swims.

a901.text: Be the frog! Shrink down. Quietly.

a902.text: You are a frog. You sit on a leaf, on land.

a903.text: Your skin is moist. It stops you from drying out.

a905.text: You are under water. Your strong legs and webbed feet push you along.

a906.text: Here, you breathe through your skin.

a907.text: Back on land, you breathe with your lungs as well.

a908.text: Land and water. Both are home.

a1003.text: Amphibians are animals that can live both on land and in water. Amphibians usually have four legs.

a1004.text: Amphibians can breathe through their skin as well as their lungs.

a1005.text: They have protective moist skin to prevent them from drying out when they are on land.

a1006.text: Amphibians lay their eggs in water.

a1007.text: Frogs, toads and salamanders are amphibians.

a1008.text: So the frog is an amphibian!

a1101.text: My rule! If it swims, it is a fish. A frog swims. A duck swims. So they are fish!

a1102.text: Something is not right. If you can spot it, cross your arms. Hold on!

a1103.text: Arms crossed? One finger up! Many animals swim. To find the group, look at the outer covering.

a1104.text: Oops. I must check the cover first!

a1201.text: Show me your score hand! More than two? You beat the Buddies. Three fingers? High five!

a1202.text: Did you spot the duck? It was behind the boardwalk rail! Tell someone at home.

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?

a1301.text: Next: this animal has fins. But it hops about on the mud! Is it a fish, or an amphibian? Find out in Part Two!
